sentences.text:
Through: Mr. Utkarsh, App 
 Psi Ankita, P.S.
 R-2 in person.
Coram:
Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Sudhir Kumar Jain

The present petition is filed under section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR bearing no.0047/2019 dated 15.02.2019 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Tigri along with consequential proceedings.
2. Issue notice.
3. Mr. Utkarsh, Additional Public Prosecutor assisted by PSI Ankita, P.S. Tigri, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent no.1/State.
The respondent no.2 is present in person and accepts notice.

4. The petitioner and the respondent no.2 got married on 05.12.2015 at Delhi according Hindu rites and customs and out of their marriage, one girl child, namely, Purva was born on 03.03.2018, who at present is under the care and custody of the respondent no. 2.
The petitioner and the respondent no.2 due to matrimonial differences started to live separately since July, 2018 without any cohabitation.
This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 due to matrimonial differences, filed petitions under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and under section 125 Cr.P.C. besides one petition for custody of the child.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is stated that these petitions have already been withdrawn/disposed of.

6. The respondent no. 2 also got registered FIR bearing no.0047/2019 under sections 406/498A/34 IPC at P.S. Tigri wherein besides petitioner, his family members i.e. father, mother and two sisters,
namely, Umesh, Munni Devi, Manika Singh @ Ruby and Ritu, respectively, were implicated.

After conclusion of investigation, the charge-sheet was filed and the trial is stated to be pending in the court of Ms. Rashi Raheja, MM, Mahila Court, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi/Successor Court.

entities.text: Mahila Court, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner and the respondent no. 2 are identified by PSI Ankita, P.S. Tigri.

7. The petitioner and the respondent no.2 have settled their disputes vide Settlement dated 17.04.2023 whereby they have agreed to dissolve their marriage by way of mutual consent as per section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

The petitioner has agreed to pay Rs.8,00,000/-
(Rupees Eight Lacs Only) to the respondent no.2 towards full and final satisfaction of her claims/legal entitlements (past, present and future) arising out of marriage between the petitioner and the respondent no. 2 including permanent alimony/maintenance/istridhan etc. and other miscellaneous and legal expenses.
It is stated that the petitioner has already paid Rs.6,00,000/- to the respondent no.2, which is acknowledged by the respondent no.2.

The petitioner also delivered a demand draft bearing no. 003586 dated 24.08.2023 drawn on Axis Bank, amounting to Rs.2,00,000/- towards payment of balance settled amount to the respondent no.2, which is accepted This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/09/2023 at 21:21:31 by the respondent no.2.
8.

The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent no.2 has been dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 by the court of Sh. Paramjit Singh, Principal Judge, Family Court, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi vide judgment dated 08.07.2023 in petition bearing HMA no.865/2023 titled as Anjali and Rahul Kumar.

entities.text: Family Court, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. The counsel for the petitioner stated that the disputes between the petitioner and the respondent no.2 have already been settled vide Settlement dated 17.04.2023, the terms and conditions of which have already been executed.

The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent no.2 has already been dissolved as such, the present petition be allowed and FIR bearing no.0047/2019 be quashed along with consequential judicial proceedings.

10. The respondent no.2 stated that she has settled with the petitioner and his family members out of her free own will and without any force, fear or coercion and her marriage with the petitioner has already been dissolved as such, she does not have any objection if the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no.0047/2019 is quashed along with consequential judicial proceedings.

sentences.text:
The Additional Public Prosecutor stated that the petitioner and the respondent no.2 have already settled their disputes vide Settlement dated 17.04.2023 and their marriage has already been dissolved as such, he does not have any objection if the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no.0047/2019 is quashed but he expressed his concern regarding one minor daughter, namely,
Purva in view of the judgment titled as Ganesh V Sudhir This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/09/2023 at 21:21:31 Kumar Shrivastava and Ors. (2020) 20 SCC 787, and stated that the respondent no.2 can settle her claims relating to maintenance/permanent alimony/istridhan with the petitioner but she could not give up the rights which vest or shall be vesting in favour of her minor daughter namely, Purva relating to maintenance and other issues.
12. The petitioner and the respondent no. 2 got married on 05.12.2015 and due to matrimonial differences, they are living separately since July 2018 without any cohabitation.

The petitioner and the respondent no.2 have already settled their pending disputes vide Settlement dated 17.04.2023,
the terms and conditions of which have already been executed and the respondent no.2 has already received the entire settled amount.
The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent no. 2 has already been dissolved as detailed hereinabove.

No useful purpose shall be served if the proceedings arising out of FIR bearing no.0047/2019 are allowed to be continued and it would be an exercise in futility.
13.

After considering all facts and in the interest of parties, the present petition is allowed and FIR bearing no. 0047/2019 dated 15.02.2019 registered under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Tigri along with consequential proceedings including judicial proceedings stated to be pending in the court of Ms. Rashi Raheja, MM, Mahila Court, South District, Saket Courts, Delhi/Successor Court is quashed.
